types.name: Key material
types.desc: User key material, the 32-byte wrapping key, wrapped or unwrapped master and HMAC keys, salts and IVs used to derive or apply them.

types.name: Physical payload
types.desc: abd_t: block bytes as stored (ciphertext, or plaintext with a MAC) or their decrypted form.

types.name: ARC buffer
types.desc: arc_buf_t / arc_buf_hdr_t: cached block handed to a consumer.

types.name: Block pointer
types.desc: blkptr_t fields: here the salt, IV and MAC stored in it.

types.name: Transaction
types.desc: A sync task queued for a txg.

types.name: Control
types.desc: Calls that carry no key or payload: lookups, checks, holds and releases, errors. Draw dashed.

contexts.name: Kernel, in the thread of the calling process (an ioctl on /dev/zfs, mount(2) or umount(2)) or a helper thread it starts, outside syncing context and outside any dmu_tx
Syncing context: txg_sync thread, one txg at a time (sync tasks run here)
zio issue taskq: CPU work such as encryption
zio interrupt taskq: completion processing such as decryption
Runs in whichever context calls it

nodes.title: Administrator
nodes.role: The person or script typing the command. Every path in this graph that a command starts begins with a wire from this node; the arrows that come back into a command node are its results, errors and refusals.

nodes.title: zfs(8) command
nodes.role: The administrator's entry points: `zfs create`, `zfs load-key` and `zfs unload-key` (`-r` and `-a` act only on encryption roots not already in the wanted state; `-n` only verifies the key; `-L` overrides keylocation), `zfs change-key` (`-l` loads the current key first, `-i` inherits the parent's key, `-o` sets keyformat, keylocation or pbkdf2iters) and `zfs send -w`.

nodes.title: libzfs mount / unmount

ref.code: share_mount_one(zfs_handle_t *zhp, int op, int flags, enum sa_protocol protocol,

nodes.role: `zfs mount -l` sets MS_CRYPT: if the dataset's keystatus is unavailable, the key of its encryption root is loaded before mount(2). Without `-l` such a mount fails with "encryption key not loaded". `zfs unmount -u` also sets MS_CRYPT: after unmounting an encryption root whose key is loaded, it unloads the key.

nodes.title: libzfs key operations
nodes.role: Policy checks before any ioctl. Create: a dataset given keyformat (keylocation defaults to prompt) becomes a new encryption root; one given neither inherits its encrypted parent's key, even with a different encryption suite. Load and unload work only on an encryption root. change-key refuses clones and needs the current key loaded; `-i` needs an encryption root whose parent is encrypted and has its key loaded.

nodes.title: Key material (keylocation)
nodes.role: Reads the user's key from keylocation: `prompt` (the terminal, or stdin when it is not a terminal), `file://`, or `http(s)://`. At a terminal a new key is asked for twice; raw keys cannot be typed. Checks the format: raw exactly 32 bytes, hex exactly 64 hex digits, a new passphrase 8 to 512 characters.

nodes.title: Wrapping key derivation
nodes.role: Turns key material into the 32-byte wrapping key, in userspace: the kernel never sees a passphrase. raw: used as is. hex: decoded. passphrase: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 with the dataset's 64-bit pbkdf2salt and pbkdf2iters iterations, deliberately slow. Every new passphrase key gets a new random salt; pbkdf2iters defaults to 350000 and the kernel refuses fewer than 100000.

nodes.title: libzfs_core

ref.code: lzc_create(const char *fsname, enum lzc_dataset_type type, nvlist_t *props,

nodes.role: Packs the arguments into nvlists for /dev/zfs. The wrapping key travels as the uint8 array `wkeydata` inside the `hidden_args` nvlist, which is stripped before the command is written to pool history.

nodes.title: Create and key ioctls
nodes.role: Kernel entry for ZFS_IOC_CREATE, ZFS_IOC_LOAD_KEY, ZFS_IOC_UNLOAD_KEY and ZFS_IOC_CHANGE_KEY. The key commands refuse snapshot names (containing `@` or `%`).

nodes.title: dsl_crypto_params
nodes.role: Builds a dsl_crypto_params_t from the ioctl nvlists: the command, the encryption suite (`on` means aes-256-gcm), keylocation, and a dsl_wrapping_key_t holding the 32-byte key with its keyformat, salt and iteration count. encryption, keyformat, pbkdf2salt and pbkdf2iters are removed from the property list: they live in the DSL Crypto Key, not as ordinary dataset properties.

nodes.title: Dataset opened for decryption
nodes.role: Mounting a file system (`zfsvfs_create()`) or opening a zvol owns the dataset with decrypt set. DS_HOLD_FLAG_DECRYPT creates a key mapping, which fails with EACCES when the key is not loaded. If the objset block is still unauthenticated, its MACs are checked here. Disowning at unmount removes the mapping. Raw send holds datasets without decrypt and needs no key.

nodes.title: spa_keystore_load_wkey()
nodes.role: `zfs load-key` in the kernel. The dataset must be its own encryption root (EINVAL otherwise). The offered key is proved by unwrapping this dataset's DSL Crypto Key; its keyformat, salt and iterations are then taken from that key object. With noop (`-n`) it stops there. Otherwise the wrapping key is inserted in the keystore and zvols under the dataset are created. No master key stays in memory.

nodes.title: spa_keystore_unload_wkey()
nodes.role: `zfs unload-key` in the kernel. Waits for a txg sync so that pending writes drop their key holds, then removes the wrapping key: EACCES if it is not loaded, EBUSY while any DSL Crypto Key still holds it (some dataset under this encryption root is still mounted or open with decryption). The key is zeroed and freed and zvol device nodes under the dataset are removed.

nodes.title: Master key unwrap
nodes.role: Reads the DSL Crypto Key object and decrypts the master key and HMAC key with the wrapping key, using the dataset's cipher mode (GCM or CCM) with the key guid, suite and version as authenticated data. A MAC failure means the wrong wrapping key and returns EACCES. On success a fresh random salt is chosen and the current data key is derived from the master key with HKDF-SHA512.

nodes.title: Wrapping key tree (sk_wkeys)
nodes.role: Loaded wrapping keys, one per encryption root, keyed by the root's dsl_dir object number. A dataset finds its wrapping key by reading the root's object number from its own DSL Crypto Key; this lookup is all that "inheriting the key" means. Refcounted: every in-memory master key holds its wrapping key. keystatus is `available` exactly when this lookup succeeds.

nodes.title: DSL Crypto Key tree (sk_dsl_keys)
nodes.role: Unwrapped master keys in memory, one per DSL Crypto Key object and refcounted, so snapshots and clones that share a key object share this entry. A hold that misses the tree unwraps the key from disk with the encryption root's wrapping key. At refcount zero the key is zeroed and freed and its hold on the wrapping key is dropped.

nodes.title: Key mapping tree (sk_key_mappings)
nodes.role: Maps a dataset object number to its master key. Created when a dataset is held with decryption, released when it is released or disowned. Every encrypt, decrypt and MAC operation looks its key up here by the block's objset id; no mapping means EACCES.

nodes.title: spa_sync()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Creating an encrypted dataset and changing a key are DSL sync tasks: `dsl_sync_task()` runs the check function in the caller, then the caller waits while `spa_sync()` (through `dsl_pool_sync()`) runs the check again and then the sync function, so the change lands atomically in one txg.

nodes.title: Encrypted dataset creation

ref.code: dmu_objset_create(const char *name, dmu_objset_type_t type, uint64_t flags,

nodes.role: Check: without a new key the dataset must inherit from an encrypted parent whose key is loaded (EACCES otherwise); a new key needs a valid keylocation and keyformat, and a passphrase key a salt and at least 100000 iterations. Needs the encryption and bookmark_v2 features. Sync: a clone takes a reference on its origin's key object; any other encrypted dataset gets a new key object of its own, wrapped with its new wrapping key or with its parent's. A new wrapping key is then loaded into the keystore.

nodes.title: spa_keystore_change_key()
nodes.role: `zfs change-key` as a sync task. Check: the dataset is encrypted and not a clone, the suite is not being changed, the current key is loaded, and every key object that will be rewrapped unwraps with its root's key (ZFS_ERR_CRYPTO_KEY_MISMATCH otherwise). Sync: walks the dataset and every descendant whose encryption root is the same (clones are skipped: they share their origin's key object), rewraps each master key under the new wrapping key and records the new encryption root, then replaces the dataset's wrapping key entry. `-i` does the same with the parent's wrapping key and clears keylocation.

nodes.title: New master key
nodes.role: Creates the DSL Crypto Key ZAP object in the MOS and a random master key (as long as the suite's key: 16, 24 or 32 bytes), a 64-byte HMAC key, a key guid and a first salt. This master key is kept for the life of the dataset and its snapshots. A clone does not get one: it only increments the reference count of its origin's key object.

nodes.title: Wrap and store master key
nodes.role: Encrypts the master key and HMAC key with the wrapping key under a new random 96-bit IV, and writes the result with its 128-bit MAC into the key object together with the suite, the encryption root's object number, the key guid, and the wrapping key's keyformat, pbkdf2salt and pbkdf2iters. This is all that a change-key rewrites.

nodes.title: DSL Crypto Key object (MOS)
nodes.role: One ZAP object per encrypted dataset directory, shared by its snapshots and, through a reference count, by its clones. Lives in the MOS, which is not encrypted. Holds the wrapped master and HMAC keys, wrapping IV and MAC, suite, key guid, version, encryption root object number, and keyformat, pbkdf2salt and pbkdf2iters. `zfs get` reads encryptionroot, keyformat and pbkdf2iters from here. Destroyed with the last dataset that references it.

nodes.title: dbuf_sync_leaf() / dbuf_write()

ref.code: dmu_write_policy(objset_t *os, dnode_t *dn, int level, int wp, zio_prop_t *zp)

nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. `dmu_write_policy()` marks every block of an encrypted objset for ENCRYPT. Blocks of encrypted object types keep at most two copies (the third DVA slot holds the salt and IV) and never use nop-write; dedup is allowed only for encrypted types.

nodes.title: dbuf_read()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. A normal read asks the ARC for decrypted data. DMU_READ_NO_DECRYPT (raw receive) reads protected blocks raw instead. A cached buffer that is still encrypted or unauthenticated is passed through `arc_untransform()` before it is returned.

nodes.title: arc_read()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Without ZIO_FLAG_RAW_ENCRYPT a miss reads the block through a pipeline that decrypts it, and the header keeps the plaintext. With it (raw send, dnode prefetch) the header keeps the ciphertext. Blocks that are only authenticated are always read without checking the MAC; the check is deferred until a consumer fills a buffer with the key loaded.

nodes.title: arc_buf (consumer copy)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Filling a consumer buffer from a protected header: if only ciphertext is cached, `arc_hdr_decrypt()` decrypts it into the header's plaintext copy for this and later hits; if the block was not yet authenticated, `arc_hdr_authenticate()` checks its MAC when the key is loaded and otherwise leaves it unauthenticated. Decryption and MAC errors reach the consumer as EIO.

nodes.title: ENCRYPT
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Runs after WRITE_COMPRESS, only for newly allocated blocks (and rewritten ZIL blocks). Level-0 blocks of encrypted types are encrypted; other object types in an encrypted objset are authenticated with an HMAC and stay plaintext; indirect blocks store a SHA-512 of their children's MACs; the objset block carries two HMACs. A raw write (raw receive) stores the supplied salt, IV and MAC without using a key.

nodes.title: READ_BP_INIT
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. For a protected block read without ZIO_FLAG_RAW_ENCRYPT, and for every indirect block of an encrypted objset, pushes `zio_decrypt()` as a transform that runs when the read completes.

nodes.title: DONE
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. `zio_pop_transforms()` runs `zio_decrypt()`: an indirect block has its child-MAC checksum verified (no key needed), an authenticated block its HMAC, an encrypted block is decrypted. A MAC mismatch becomes EIO with an authentication ereport; a missing key is EACCES.

nodes.title: spa_do_crypt_abd() and MAC helpers

ref.code: spa_do_crypt_mac_abd(boolean_t generate, spa_t *spa, uint64_t dsobj, abd_t *abd,

nodes.role: The bridge from the zio and ARC layers to the keystore. Looks up the dataset's master key by objset id, holds it for the call, and runs the operation. When encrypting a normal block it obtains the current salt and a random IV; a dedup block gets salt and IV from an HMAC of its plaintext, so equal blocks encrypt equally; a ZIL block got its salt and IV when its log block was allocated.

nodes.title: Salt and IV
nodes.role: Data keys are per salt, not per block: one 64-bit salt and the key derived from it serve many blocks. Every use is counted; after zfs_key_max_salt_uses blocks (default 400,000,000, which is also the maximum) a new random salt is chosen and a new key derived with HKDF. Every unwrap also starts with a fresh salt. The IV is 96 random bits per block.

nodes.title: AES-GCM / AES-CCM

ref.code: zio_crypt_init_uios(boolean_t encrypt, uint64_t version, dmu_object_type_t ot,

nodes.role: Picks the data key for the block's salt: the cached current key if the salt is current, otherwise `hkdf_sha512()` of the master key and that salt. Encrypts or decrypts with AES-GCM or AES-CCM (on QAT hardware when available) and produces or checks a 128-bit MAC. In dnode blocks only the bonus buffers are encrypted; in ZIL blocks the parts needed to claim the log stay plaintext and are covered as authenticated data.

nodes.title: HMACs and MAC checksums
nodes.role: Authentication without encryption. Unencrypted object types: HMAC-SHA512 with the dataset's HMAC key, truncated to 128 bits. Objset block: a portable MAC (root of the MAC tree in the meta-dnode) and a local MAC (user accounting), 256 bits each, kept inside the block. Indirect blocks: a SHA-512 of their children's MACs, which needs no key, so a raw send can carry the tree without the master key.

nodes.title: Crypto fields in the block pointer
nodes.role: Where per-block crypto state lives: the 64-bit salt in the first word of DVA[2], the 96-bit IV in the second word of DVA[2] plus the upper 32 bits of blk_fill, and the 128-bit MAC in the second half of blk_cksum; the first half keeps a truncated checksum of the stored bytes, which needs no key. The objset block keeps its MACs inside the block and a ZIL block in its log chain header.

nodes.title: Raw send (zfs send -w)

ref.code: dmu_send(const char *tosnap, const char *fromsnap, boolean_t embedok,

nodes.role: Sends blocks exactly as stored, so no key needs to be loaded and the stream stays encrypted. The DRR_BEGIN payload carries `crypt_keydata`: the master and HMAC keys still wrapped, with their IV and MAC, suite, key guid and version, the encryption root's keyformat, pbkdf2salt and pbkdf2iters, the portable objset MAC, the meta-dnode layout and IVset guids. Each DRR_WRITE carries its block's salt, IV and MAC. Stream details are in the send/receive graph.

nodes.title: Raw receive

ref.code: dsl_crypto_recv_raw(const char *poolname, uint64_t dsobj, uint64_t fromobj,

nodes.role: A full raw stream creates the dataset without a key, then a sync task writes a key object holding the received wrapped keys unchanged; the dataset becomes its own encryption root with keylocation=prompt and keystatus unavailable, and loads with the sender's key. Blocks are written raw with the stream's salt, IV and MAC. On an incremental receive into a dataset whose encryption root is another dataset, the key object is only rewritten if that root's keyformat, salt and iterations match the stream's.

dsl_crypto_populate_key_nvlist(): wrapped master and HMAC keys with IV and MAC, suite, guid, version, the root's keyformat, pbkdf2salt, pbkdf2iters, portable_mac, meta-dnode layout, IVset guids; added to DRR_BEGIN as crypt_keydata
issue_data_read(): arc_read() with ZIO_FLAG_RAW
the block exactly as stored: ciphertext, or plaintext plus MAC for an authenticated type
dmu_dump_write(): zio_crypt_decode_params_bp() and zio_crypt_decode_mac_bp() fill drr_salt, drr_iv and drr_mac of the DRR_WRITE record
the stream: DRR_BEGIN with crypt_keydata, then records with the stored bytes and their salt, IV and MAC

dsl_crypto_recv_raw() sync task -> dsl_crypto_recv_raw_key_sync(): a new dataset gets keylocation "prompt", itself as encryption root, and dsl_crypto_key_sync_impl() stores the received wrapped keys unchanged; an existing dataset gets them at the end of the receive
flush_write_batch_impl(): ZIO_FLAG_RAW and the record's salt, IV and MAC; dmu_lightweight_write_by_dnode(); at txg sync zio_encrypt() takes the ZIO_FLAG_RAW_ENCRYPT branch and uses no key
runs zfs create -o encryption=on -o keyformat=... -o keylocation=... dataset
runs zfs load-key or zfs unload-key [-r | -a]
runs zfs mount [-l] or zfs unmount [-u]
runs zfs change-key [-l] [-o keyformat=...] or zfs change-key -i
runs zfs send -w (raw) snapshot, piped into zfs receive

paths.title: Create an encrypted dataset
paths.summary: `zfs create -o encryption=on -o keyformat=passphrase pool/secret`, or a plain `zfs create pool/secret/child` under an encrypted parent. Either way the new dataset gets its own random master key; what differs is which wrapping key wraps it.
paths.ends: The dataset has a DSL Crypto Key object whose encryption root is itself (newroot) or the parent's root (inherit). Its wrapping key is loaded, so `zfs create` goes on to mount it (path mount).

options.label: New encryption root (keyformat given, own wrapping key)
Child of an encrypted parent, wrapped with the parent's encryption root key

paths.title: zfs load-key
paths.summary: Loads the wrapping key of an encryption root. Nothing is decrypted yet: the key is only proved by unwrapping the root's own master key, and that copy is thrown away again.
paths.ends: The wrapping key is in the keystore. keystatus is `available` for the root and for every dataset whose encryption root it is. No master key is in memory until a dataset is opened (path mount).

steps.note: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 over the passphrase with pbkdf2salt and pbkdf2iters: the slow step that protects against guessing
raw: the 32 bytes are the wrapping key; hex: 64 hex digits decoded to 32 bytes

paths.title: Mount: master key unwrapped, key mapping created
paths.summary: Opening a dataset for decryption is where a master key is unwrapped and bound to the dataset. From then on every block I/O of the dataset finds its key by objset id.
paths.ends: The dataset is owned with a key mapping, its objset block is authenticated, and its master key is held by the mapping (and holds the wrapping key). Reads and writes now work (paths read and write).

options.label: zfs mount -l (loads the encryption root's key first if needed, as in path load_key)
master key not in memory yet
already in memory (another open snapshot, clone or user of the same key object)

paths.title: Write a block: encrypt or authenticate
paths.summary: A dirty block of an encrypted dataset on its way to disk at txg sync. What ENCRYPT does depends on the block.
paths.ends: The block pointer carries the salt, IV and MAC (or the MAC, or the MAC checksum); CHECKSUM_GENERATE and allocation follow as in the I/O graph's path `zfs-io-flow:txg_sync`. Without a key mapping the write cannot happen, which is why unload-key waits for a txg sync and refuses while datasets are open.

options.label: Level-0 block of an encrypted type (file data, directories, dnodes, ZIL, zvol data)
Level-0 block of an unencrypted type (for example the ZFS master node): authenticated only
The objset block: two embedded HMACs
Indirect block: hash of the children's MACs

steps.note: the objset block is written the same way, by dmu_objset_sync()

paths.title: Read a block: decrypt
paths.summary: A normal (not raw) read of an encrypted block. The data key is recomputed from the master key and the salt stored in the block pointer.
paths.ends: The consumer has plaintext and the ARC header keeps a decrypted copy. With the key unloaded, the key lookup fails with EACCES; a tampered block fails its MAC and returns EIO.

options.label: ARC miss: decrypted by the read pipeline
ARC hit on a header that holds only ciphertext: decrypted by the ARC

paths.title: zfs change-key: new wrapping key, no data rewritten
paths.summary: A passphrase change, or turning a dataset that inherited its key into a new encryption root. Only the wrapped copies of the master keys are rewritten; every data block stays as it is.
paths.ends: The key objects of the dataset and of every descendant under the same encryption root hold the same master keys wrapped with the new key; the old wrapping key is freed from memory and no key object in the pool is wrapped with it any more. A raw send stream made earlier still carries the master key wrapped with the old key.

options.label: The dataset is already an encryption root (for example a new passphrase)
The dataset inherited its key and becomes a new encryption root

steps.note: keyformat and keylocation default to the current ones
keyformat is required; keylocation defaults to prompt

paths.title: zfs change-key -i: rejoin the parent's encryption root
paths.summary: An encryption root gives up its own key and wraps its master keys (and those of its descendants under it) with the parent's encryption root key.
paths.ends: encryptionroot of the dataset and its inheriting descendants is now the parent's encryption root, keylocation is cleared, and loading the parent's root key gives access to all of them.

paths.title: Unmount and zfs unload-key
paths.summary: Removing the wrapping key from memory. It only succeeds once no dataset under the encryption root still holds a master key.
paths.ends: keystatus is `unavailable`. The master keys in memory were zeroed when their last holder went away; the key objects on disk are unchanged.

options.label: zfs unload-key on datasets that are already unmounted (fails with EBUSY if one is still mounted)

paths.title: Raw send and receive (zfs send -w)
paths.summary: Replicating an encrypted dataset without its key: the blocks travel as stored and the master key travels still wrapped.
paths.ends: The received dataset is its own encryption root with keystatus `unavailable`; `zfs load-key` with the sender's passphrase or key opens it, because keyformat, pbkdf2salt and pbkdf2iters came along. Neither side decrypted anything. The stream format and receive mechanics are in the send/receive graph: `zfs-send-receive:raw_send` and `zfs-send-receive:raw_recv`.

model: There are two layers of keys. Blocks are encrypted with keys derived from a dataset's master key, which is random, never changes and never leaves the kernel unwrapped. The user's key (passphrase, raw or hex) only becomes the 32-byte wrapping key, which encrypts the master key inside the dataset's DSL Crypto Key object in the pool's meta-object set (MOS).

Because only the wrapped copy of the master key depends on the user's key, `zfs change-key` rewrites a few small key objects in one txg and no data block. The new wrapping key replaces the old one; the master keys stay the same.

An encryption root is the dataset whose wrapping key is used. A child created without its own key still gets a master key of its own, but wraps it with the root's wrapping key; its key object records the root, and the keystore finds the wrapping key through that record. Snapshots share their dataset's key object and clones share their origin's. `load-key` and `unload-key` act only on encryption roots; `change-key` can turn any dataset that is not a clone into one.

`zfs load-key` only puts the wrapping key in memory, after proving it by unwrapping the root's master key. A master key is unwrapped when a dataset is opened for decryption (mount, zvol open), and the key mapping created then is what every encrypting or decrypting I/O looks up. `unload-key` fails with EBUSY while any dataset under the root is still open.

Block encryption happens in the ENCRYPT stage, after compression: AES-GCM or AES-CCM with a random 96-bit IV and a data key derived with HKDF from the master key and a 64-bit salt. A salt (and its key) is shared by many blocks and rotated after a limit. Salt, IV and MAC are stored in the block pointer.

Not everything is encrypted. The MOS (pool metadata, including the key objects) is not encrypted at all. Inside an encrypted dataset, indirect blocks, the objset block, the core of each dnode and some object types stay readable but are authenticated (HMAC, or a hash of the children's MACs), so the pool can be scrubbed and the dataset raw-sent without keys.
A raw send (`zfs send -w`) ships the blocks as stored plus the master key still wrapped; the receiver stores both unchanged and can only read the data after `zfs load-key` with the sender's key.
simplifications: The data paths jump over pipeline stages and the vdev layer drawn in the I/O graph: `dbuf_write()` to ENCRYPT, READ_BP_INIT to DONE and the device read in between are single wires here.
A sync task's check function runs twice, once in the calling thread and once in syncing context; the diagram draws the check where its effect matters, once.
Returns are drawn only where a result or error matters; most holds and releases of keys during a single I/O are folded into the lookup wires.
ZIL encryption (salt and IV chosen at log block allocation, MAC in the log chain header), encrypted dedup and dnode bonus-buffer encryption are described in node text only.
Snapshots and clones share a key object and are not drawn separately; `zfs promote`, `zfs rename` and the forced change-key commands are left out.
The crypto back ends (ICP, Linux kernel crypto API, FreeBSD crypto, QAT) are folded into the AES-GCM / AES-CCM node.
Raw send and receive are reduced to their key data; the stream itself belongs to the send/receive graph.

page.title: ZFS Encryption Keys
page.intro: This spec describes a diagram of OpenZFS native encryption from the key's point of view: which key actually encrypts a block, how a passphrase becomes a wrapping key, how the wrapping key protects each dataset's master key in its DSL Crypto Key object, what `zfs load-key`, `zfs unload-key` and `zfs change-key` do in the kernel, why a passphrase change rewrites no data, what an encryption root is, how blocks are encrypted, decrypted and authenticated in the zio pipeline and the ARC, and what a raw send carries.
